subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Some bacteria have developed resistance to chemicals designed to kill them.
• This is known as antibiotic resistance.
• Staphylococcus bacteria develop resistance through genetic mutations.
• This helps Staphylococcus bacteria survive antibiotic treatments.
• Escherichia coli bacteria develop resistance by acquiring resistance genes from other bacteria.
• This helps E. coli bacteria survive in hostile environments.
prompt: The student wants to emphasize a difference in how Staphylococcus and E. coli bacteria develop antibiotic resistance. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Staphylococcus bacteria acquire resistance genes from other bacteria, while E. coli bacteria develop resistance through genetic mutations.
choices.B: Unlike E. coli bacteria, which develop resistance by acquiring genes from other bacteria, Staphylococcus bacteria develop resistance through genetic mutations.
choices.C: Staphylococcus and E. coli bacteria are two examples of organisms that develop antibiotic resistance.
choices.D: Bacteria that develop antibiotic resistance can survive chemicals designed to kill them.

explanation:
Choice B is correct. It contrasts antibiotic resistance development: E. coli acquires genes from other bacteria while Staphylococcus develops resistance through genetic mutations.

Why D is incorrect:

Choice D is incorrect. The sentence describes what antibiotic resistance does; it doesn't emphasize a difference in how Staphylococcus and E. coli bacteria specifically develop resistance.
